name: Saratoga Lake
blurb: A four-and-a-half-mile bass factory minutes off the Northway: milfoil flats and dock lines for largemouth, the Snake Hill dropoff over the 95 ft hole, stocked walleye at dusk, and one of the region's best crappie and ice fisheries.

launches.name: Saratoga Lake State Boat Launch (NYS OPRHP, Route 9P)
launches.notes: NYS OPRHP hard-surface launch on Route 9P at the north end. $10 vehicle fee at automated kiosk (card or exact change; NYS residents 62+ free weekdays). Launching April 1 - Nov 1; parking for up to 100 trailers plus overflow.

launches.name: Waterfront Park (City of Saratoga Springs) - cartop / kayak launch
launches.notes: Free public park on the west shore off Route 9P (Garside Lane) with a hand-launch area for canoes and kayaks, benches, picnic tables, and seasonal porta-potty. No trailer ramp - cartop craft only. Reverse-geocode of the shoreline slipway (43.0522,-73.7290) returns Garside Lane, City of Saratoga Springs, confirming the west-shore park location.

launches.name: Lee's Park Campground & Marina (fee)
launches.notes: Private campground/marina at 1466 Route 9P at the north end of the lake at the mouth of Fish Creek, immediately next to the NYS boat launch. Offers fee launching, daily and seasonal dockage, and camping. Reverse-geocode (43.0534,-73.7203) returns a parking area off Lee's Trail on the Saratoga Lake shoreline, confirming the north-end location adjacent to the state ramp.

launches.name: South Shore Marina (fee, south end)
launches.notes: Full-service marina at 113 Route 9P, Malta, at the south end of the lake. Offers fee boat-launch access (season launch passes ~$449), slips 14-26 ft, trailer storage, and mechanics. Reverse-geocode of the shoreline slipway (42.9883,-73.7582) returns 1st Street, Town of Malta, Saratoga County - confirming the south-shore Malta ramp.

launches.name: Fish Creek Marina / Kayak Shak (Staffords Bridge Road)
launches.notes: Marina and paddle-craft launch on Fish Creek (the lake's outlet) at 251 Stafford Bridge Road, about one mile downstream of the state launch. Home of the Kayak Shak (Saratoga Kayak) rentals; $10 to launch your own kayak/SUP. Dock space and boat service available. Reverse-geocode (43.0747,-73.6955) returns Staffords Bridge Road, confirming the Fish Creek outlet access point.

regsNotes.title: Largemouth & Smallmouth Bass (statewide season/limits)
regsNotes.body: Black bass (largemouth and smallmouth) on Saratoga Lake follow the NY statewide regulation: harvest season June 15 - Nov 30 with a 12-inch minimum length and a daily limit of 5. From Dec 1 - June 14 bass are catch-and-release only, artificial lures only. Saratoga Lake has a statewide reputation as a top black bass water, so expect heavy but largely catch-and-release pressure.

regsNotes.title: Northern Pike
regsNotes.body: Northern pike follow the statewide regulation on Saratoga Lake: open season May 1 - March 15, 18-inch minimum length, daily limit of 5. Pike hold along the edges of weed beds on the lake.

regsNotes.title: Walleye - statewide reg applies (NO special 18-inch reg on Saratoga)
regsNotes.body: IMPORTANT / VERIFIED: Saratoga Lake does NOT carry a walleye special regulation. The only special reg listed for Saratoga Lake in the current Region 5 special regulations is for sunfish. Walleye therefore follow the statewide rule: open season May 1 - March 15, 15-inch minimum length, daily limit of 5. (The 18-inch minimum / 3-per-day special walleye regulation exists on other NY waters such as Lake Pleasant/Sacandaga Lake and several Region 3 reservoirs, but not Saratoga Lake.) Walleye fry are stocked annually to support the fishery.

regsNotes.title: Black Crappie & White Crappie
regsNotes.body: Crappie follow the statewide regulation: open all year, 10-inch minimum length, daily limit of 25. Note the minimum is 10 inches (not 9). Saratoga Lake has a strong crappie population and a well-known spring and early-ice crappie bite.

regsNotes.title: Yellow Perch
regsNotes.body: Yellow perch follow the statewide regulation: open all year, no minimum length, daily limit of 50. Perch are a mainstay of the winter ice fishery, typically taken in 10-20 feet of water on tip-ups with minnows or small jigs.

regsNotes.title: Sunfish - Saratoga Lake SPECIAL regulation
regsNotes.body: Saratoga Lake (and lower Fish Creek) has an 8-inch minimum / 15-per-day sunfish reg - part of DEC's Big Panfish Initiative (adopted 2021), an experimental program to improve sunfish size structure. The study window is closing and the reg could be revised when BPI concludes; verify the Region 5 specials each April 1. Statewide default elsewhere: 25/day, no minimum.

regsNotes.title: Baitfish rules - certified bait is fine here
regsNotes.body: There are no baitfish use restrictions listed specifically for Saratoga Lake, so the general statewide baitfish rules apply: you may use legal baitfish, but baitfish bought must come from a licensed/certified dealer (green tag), and personally collected baitfish may only be used on the same water where taken unless you carry a receipt. A baitfish license is required to sell baitfish. Circle hooks are required when fishing with baitfish. Ice anglers commonly use fathead minnows and 'cup' (mousie/spike) baits here.

regsNotes.title: Ice fishing - permitted, watch thin ice near Fish Creek outlet
regsNotes.body: Ice fishing is permitted on Saratoga Lake and on all Saratoga County waters except where trout inhabit. Up to 7 ice-fishing lines (tip-ups/jigging combined) are allowed per angler. Ice is unreliable near the north-end Fish Creek outlet and the mouth of Kayaderosseras Creek where current keeps water open; anglers report open water in these areas even when Brown's Beach and Fitch Road access still hold safe ice. Always verify thickness before venturing out.

regsNotes.title: Kayaderosseras Creek spring closure
regsNotes.body: Kayaderosseras Creek, the lake's main tributary and a walleye spawning run, is closed to all fishing from March 16 through April 30 (from Saratoga Lake upstream to the first railroad bridge). This protects spawning walleye. Plan spring walleye trips on the main lake, not the creek.

regsNotes.title: Invasive species / milfoil - clean-drain-dry (no mandatory inspection)
regsNotes.body: Unlike Lake George, Saratoga Lake has no mandatory boat-inspection/decontamination stations, but Eurasian watermilfoil and curly-leaf pondweed are established and both re-root from stem fragments. NY law requires cleaning, draining, and drying boats and trailers between waters; ice anglers should clean gear and dispose of plant fragments in the trash, not the water. The Saratoga Lake Protection & Improvement District (SLPID) manages milfoil and lake use.

localColor.note: Saratoga Lake is one of the most heavily fished waters in all of New York, ranking 15th statewide in angler days with an estimated ~201,385 angler days of effort. It carries a statewide reputation as a quality black bass and sunfish water.

It really is a bass factory: DEC's 2015 boat-angler creel survey found black bass (overwhelmingly largemouth) accounted for about 78% of total fishing effort, with an estimated 20,989 bass caught. Notably about 85% of legal-sized (12-inch) bass were released - a strong catch-and-release culture.

Saratoga is one of DEC's Big Panfish Initiative study lakes: the 8-inch/15-fish sunfish reg (2021) is being tested here, and DEC's 2022 netting survey says it's working on an exceptional fishery - bluegill PSD 98.5 with fish to 11.4 inches.

Walleye are sustained by stocking: DEC puts roughly 13 million walleye fry in the lake annually, a policy running since 1979. The stocking location was changed after the thin 2015 survey; a 2027 percid survey will judge whether it worked.

Ice fishing is a big part of the lake's culture, with a strong walleye, perch and crappie hard-water following. Winter reports describe perch in 10-20 ft on tip-ups and small jigs, and the classic advice to 'not overwork your bait this time of year - sometimes the absence of movement triggers the strike.'

The famous spring crappie run draws crowds: crappie fishing was a close second to bass in effort during May in the creel survey. Anglers key on shallow spawning bays and dock lines (Manning's Cove area is a well-known spot) with small jigs under floats.

Newer than the 2015 creel survey: DEC's April 2022 trap-net survey found black crappie the most-caught species (27.8/net-night, to 12.8 inches, relative weight 110) and an outstanding bluegill size structure - 'healthy and well balanced,' with excellent angling expected 'for the foreseeable future.'

Weed management shapes the weedline bite now: ProcellaCOR treatments have knocked milfoil in treated zones to roughly 1-2 percent of prior coverage, and the 2026 harvest opened June 1 off Snake Hill and the south end with five no-cut herbicide zones. Expect thinner edges in treated areas and fresh-cut lanes elsewhere.
Still a club-circuit staple: USA Bassin's Adirondack Division opened its 2026 Saratoga round on May 3 (won by Ben Bornhorst), alongside rounds on Champlain, the Hudson, and Lake George.

Hard-water benchmark: winter 2024-25 ran ice-in Jan 11 to ice-out Mar 21. No reliable record surfaced for 2025-26 (the long-running local ice report is defunct), so verify current ice locally before walking.

spots.name: South End Weed Flats (off Brown's Beach)
spots.structure: Broad shallow south-basin flats with thick milfoil/coontail beds; weed edges in 5-10 ft breaking to 10-14 ft; soft bottom with scattered hard patches

seasons.spr: Ice-out crappie and perch over emerging weeds 6-12 ft; pre-spawn largemouth move onto the flats as water warms
seasons.sum: Prime largemouth water in and along the weeds; pike on the weed edges early and late Note: SLPID's harvester works this end from early June and part of the Brown's Beach-to-South Shore stretch is a herbicide no-cut zone - weed edges move year to year with cutting and ProcellaCOR milfoil treatment, so relocate the live outside edge each trip.
seasons.fall: Bass regroup on isolated green weed clumps 2-10 ft; perch school on the flats
seasons.ice: One of the lake's busiest ice areas; weeds off Brown's Beach hold crappie and perch, tip-ups take pike

seasons.fall: Walleye slide onto the rocky point at dusk; smallmouth on the deep rock-to-weed transitions
seasons.ice: Weeds from Snake Hill south hold panfish; deep break is a walleye/crappie jigging area

seasons.ice: Protected cove ice forms early; panfish in the weeds, tip-ups for pike
